questions.label: Exercise 1
questions.prompt:
Write a program that loops 5 times.
Each time round the loop, ask the user to enter a number.
If the number is greater than 0, print "Positive".
Otherwise, print "Negative".
questions.starter:
# Loop 5 times
# Ask user for a number each time
# Print Positive or Negative
questions.scheme:
Award 1 mark for a correct for loop that runs 5 times.
Award 1 mark for asking the user to input a number inside the loop (using int() with input()).
Award 1 mark for a correct if/else inside the loop that prints the right message based on whether the number is greater than 0.

questions.label: Exercise 2

- Loops 4 times, asking the user for a number each time.
- If the number entered is greater than 10, adds 1 to the counter.
- After the loop, prints how many numbers were greater than 10.
questions.starter:
# Set counter to 0
# Loop 4 times
# Check if each number is > 10 and update counter
# Print the final counter
questions.scheme:
Award 1 mark for setting the counter to 0 before the loop.
Award 1 mark for a correct for loop that runs 4 times.

Award 1 mark for adding 1 to the counter when the condition is true, and printing the counter after the loop.

questions.label: Exercise 3
questions.prompt:
A teacher wants to find out how many students passed and failed a test.
A pass is a score of 50 or more.

Write a program that:
- Sets two counters to 0: one for passes, one for fails.
- Loops 5 times, asking the user for a score each time.
- If the score is 50 or more, adds 1 to the passes counter.
- Otherwise, adds 1 to the fails counter.
- After the loop, prints both the number of passes and the number of fails.
questions.starter:
# Set passes and fails counters to 0
# Loop 5 times
# Check each score and update the correct counter
# Print passes and fails
questions.scheme:
Award 1 mark for setting both counters (passes and fails) to 0 before the loop.
Award 1 mark for a correct loop that runs 5 times.
Award 1 mark for asking the user to input a score inside the loop.
Award 1 mark for correctly using if/else to check whether the score is 50 or more and updating the right counter.
Award 1 mark for printing both the passes and fails values after the loop.

questions.label: Exercise 4
questions.prompt:
A shopper wants to track their spending.
Items costing more than £20 are classed as expensive; anything else is cheap.

Write a program that:
- Asks the user how many items they bought.
- Sets two totals to 0: one for expensive items, one for cheap items.
- Loops that many times, asking for the price of each item.
- If the price is more than 20, adds it to the expensive total.
- Otherwise, adds it to the cheap total.
- After the loop, prints both totals.
questions.starter:
# Ask how many items
# Set expensiveTotal and cheapTotal to 0
# Loop that many times
# Add each price to the correct total
# Print both totals
questions.scheme:
Award 1 mark for asking the user for the number of items and using that value to control the loop.
Award 1 mark for setting both totals (expensiveTotal and cheapTotal) to 0 before the loop.
Award 1 mark for asking for the price of each item inside the loop.
Award 1 mark for correctly using if/else to add the price to the right total based on whether it is greater than 20.
Award 1 mark for printing both totals after the loop.
questions.example:
numItems = int(input("How many items did you buy? "))
expensiveTotal = 0
cheapTotal = 0

for x in range(numItems):
    price = float(input("Enter the price of item " + str(x + 1) + ": "))
    if price > 20:
        expensiveTotal = expensiveTotal + price
    else:
        cheapTotal = cheapTotal + price

print("Total spent on expensive items: £" + str(expensiveTotal))
print("Total spent on cheap items: £" + str(cheapTotal))

questions.label: Exercise 5
questions.prompt:
A weather station records the temperature every day for a week.
Write a program that:
- Sets two counters to 0: one for hot days (above 15°C) and one for freezing days (below 0°C).
- Loops 7 times, asking the user to enter the temperature for each day.
- If the temperature is above 15, adds 1 to the hot days counter.
- If the temperature is below 0, adds 1 to the freezing days counter.
- After the loop, prints how many hot days and how many freezing days there were.

Hint: You will need to use both if and elif here.
questions.starter:
# Set hotDays and freezingDays counters to 0
# Loop 7 times
# Check each temperature and update the correct counter
# Print both counters
questions.scheme:
Award 1 mark for setting both counters (hotDays and freezingDays) to 0 before the loop.
Award 1 mark for a correct loop that runs 7 times.
Award 1 mark for asking the user for a temperature inside the loop.
Award 1 mark for correctly using if and elif (not two separate if statements) to check both conditions and update the right counter.
Award 1 mark for printing both counters after the loop with meaningful output.
